title: Eclipse of Aug 12, 2026
brief: A definitive, verified guide to the total solar eclipse of 12 August 2026 — the first totality over mainland Europe since 1999. Hand-drawn SVG cartography of the path across Greenland, Iceland, the Atlantic and northern Spain (limits, centre line and UT ticks from the NASA/GSFC path tables, Natural Earth coastlines), an enlarged plate of the Iberian crossing, a live countdown to totality, a seven-city timetable (Paris, Madrid, Reykjavík, A Coruña, Zaragoza, Valencia, Palma) whose contact times are recomputed live in the browser with astronomy-engine and cross-checked against timeanddate and NASA sources, the minute-by-minute choreography of totality with engraved phase figures, ISO 12312-2 eye-safety rules, a travel plan weighing totality length against August cloud climatology, a to-scale diagram of how low the eclipsed Sun hangs, and the Perseid encore that peaks the same moonless night. Every dated fact verified 3 July 2026; sources cited on-sheet.
da: Observatory almanac — chalk-ecru paper, engraved near-black cartographic linework and hachured land, one solar-orange accent reserved for the Sun and the totality band, Newsreader serif, hairline graticules, small-caps labels; a 19th-century celestial atlas redrawn with modern precision.
